'''Sisir Kumar Sarkar''' ([[Bengali language|Bengali]]: শিশির কুমার সরকার; born 25 April 1953) is an Indian [[Bengali people|Bengali]] scientist associated with the [[Bhabha Atomic Research Center]].<ref name="BARC 1">{{cite web | url=http://www.barc.gov.in/publications/nl/2008/20081051.pdf | title= LASER SEPARATION OF SULPHUR – 33 ISOTOPE : A NOVEL TWO-STAGE APPROACH| publisher=BARC |year=2014 | access-date=15 November 2014}}</ref><ref name="Nano science and engineering by ionizing radiations">{{cite web | url=https://www.vbripress.com/aml/uploadsnew/8401.pdf | title=Nano science and engineering by ionizing radiations | publisher=BARC | year=2013 | access-date=15 November 2013 | archive-date=3 March 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210303211844/https://www.vbripress.com/aml/uploadsnew/8401.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref> He is best known for his contributions to photo-[[physics]] and [[photochemistry]] in nuclear fuel cycle and chemical dynamics.<ref name="BARC 2">{{cite web | url=http://www.barc.gov.in/publications/nl/2008/20081051.pdf | title= LASER SEPARATION OF SULPHUR – 33 ISOTOPE : A NOVEL TWO-STAGE APPROACH| publisher=BARC |year=2014 | access-date=15 November 2014}}</ref>

==Biography==
Sarkar was born on April 25, 1953, in [[Medinipur, West Bengal]], India. He obtained his [[Bachelor of Science]] from [[Presidency University, Kolkata|Presidency University]] and [[Master of Science]] from [[University of Calcutta]] respectively. He received his [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree from the [[University of Mumbai]] and subsequently a postdoctoral fellowship from [[Columbia University]] in 1973.<ref name="BARC 3">{{cite web | url=https://www.barc.gov.in/publications/nl/2008/20081051.pdf | title=LASER SEPARATION OF SULPHUR – 33 ISOTOPE : A NOVEL TWO-STAGE APPROACH | publisher=BARC | year=2014 | access-date=15 November 2014 | archive-date=13 April 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210413122920/https://www.barc.gov.in/publications/nl/2008/20081051.pdf | url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref><ref name="mahascience">{{cite web | url=http://mahascience.org/files/fellowship/files/academymembers.htm|title= mahascience | publisher=BARC |year=2014 | access-date=15 December 2014}}</ref> His postdoctoral work was with Prof. J.W Flynn in the area of chemical dynamics using high-resolution semiconductor diode lasers.<ref name="BARC 4">{{cite web | url=http://www.barc.gov.in/publications/nl/2008/20081051.pdf | title= LASER SEPARATION OF SULPHUR – 33 ISOTOPE : A NOVEL TWO-STAGE APPROACH| publisher=BARC |year=2014 | access-date=15 November 2014}}</ref> His siblings include the noted physicist professor of [[University of Calcutta]], Prof. Samir K Sarkar, the noted solid-state physicist of [[Presidency University, Kolkata|Presidency University]], Prof. Salil K. Sarkar and his nephew is the internationally published poet and [[microelectronics]] engineer, Sreyash Sarkar.

Sarkar joined the Multidisciplinary Research Scheme (MDRS) of [[Bhabha Atomic Research Center]], [[Mumbai]] in 1974 and started working as an A-grade scientist and in 2000 started heading the Radiation & Photochemistry Division. He has been heading several high-end projects of BARC such as the Laser Isotope Separation programme of the [[Department of Atomic Energy]] at its very onset.<ref name="ISRAPS 1">{{cite web | url=http://www.israps.org.in/pdf/2009-Vol%2021-Issue%202-3.pdf| title= ISRAPS |  publisher=ISRAPS |year=2009 | access-date=15 December 2009}}</ref> He was president of the Society of Materials Chemistry of BARC from 2013 to 2014.<ref name="SMC">{{cite web | url=https://www.smcindia.org/pdf/SMC%20Bulletin(-Vol-4-(3)-December-2013.pdf| title= SMC | publisher=SMC |year=2013 | access-date=15 December 2013}}</ref> Sarkar has also been the Vice President of ISRAPS (Indian Society for Radiation and Photochemical Sciences) and Indian Laser Association (ILA) from 2009 to 2012<ref name="ISRAPS 2">{{cite web | url=http://www.israps.org.in/pdf/2009-Vol%2021-Issue%202-3.pdf| title= ISRAPS | publisher=ISRAPS |year=2009 | access-date=15 December 2009}}</ref> and has been inducted as an executive member into the [[Maharashtra Academy of Sciences]] since 2005.<ref name="mahascience 2">{{cite web | url=http://mahascience.org/files/fellowship/files/academymembers.htm| title= Maharashtra Academy of Sciences| publisher=BARC |year=2014 | access-date=15 December 2014}}</ref> Sarkar was one of the founding members of Indian Association of Nuclear Chemists and Allied Scientists(IANCAS).<ref name="IANCAS">{{cite web | url=http://www.iancas.org.in/bulletins/October%202005.pdf| title= IANCAS | publisher=IANCAS |year=2005 | access-date=15 December 2005}}</ref>

He has worked extensively as visiting scientists at the P.N.Lebedev Physical Institute & Institute of Spectroscopy, Russia, [[Kyoto Institute of Technology]], Japan, [[Institute of Chemical Process Fundamentals]], Czech Republic, [[Paris-Sud University]], France and the [[Heidelberg University]], Germany with various laser systems including Free Electron Lasers.<ref name="ISRAPS 3">{{cite web | url=http://www.israps.org.in/pdf/2009-Vol%2021-Issue%202-3.pdf|title= ISRAPS | publisher=ISRAPS |year=2009 | access-date=15 December 2009}}</ref><ref name="Nano science and engineering by ionizing radiations-2">{{cite web | url=https://www.vbripress.com/aml/uploadsnew/8401.pdf | title=Nano science and engineering by ionizing radiations | publisher=BARC | year=2013 | access-date=15 November 2013 | archive-date=3 March 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210303211844/https://www.vbripress.com/aml/uploadsnew/8401.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Sarkar currently serves as a senior professor at [[Homi Bhabha National Institute]].<ref name="Nano science and engineering by ionizing radiations-3">{{cite web | url=https://www.vbripress.com/aml/uploadsnew/8401.pdf | title=Nano science and engineering by ionizing radiations | publisher=BARC | year=2013 | access-date=15 November 2013 | archive-date=3 March 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210303211844/https://www.vbripress.com/aml/uploadsnew/8401.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Research ==
Sarkar's research interests focused on radiation & photochemistry with lasers and accelerators, chemical dynamics, spectroscopy and laser development. He is the author or co-author of more than 350 journal articles, as well as 16 books and, 32 book chapters.<ref name="ISRAPS 4">{{cite web | url=http://www.israps.org.in/pdf/2009-Vol%2021-Issue%202-3.pdf| title= ISRAPS |publisher=ISRAPS |year=2009 | access-date=15 December 2009}}</ref>

During his tenure as head of the Radiation & Photochemistry Division at BARC, he launched the Molecular Laser Isotope Separation (MLIS) programme with the aid of [[Department of Atomic Energy]] in close collaboration with the [[International Nuclear Information System]](INIS). The idea was to use the intense, monochromatic light of lasers to break the chemical bonds of only those molecules containing the fissionable isotope uranium-235. At present the programme is evolving around the separation of low and middle mass isotopes, namely sulphur 34/33/32, oxygen 17/18, carbon 13/12, hydrogen T/D/H to be followed by an advanced engineering programme designed to lead to a demonstration plant. The latest results have come very close to the design parameters specified for a full-scale separation of carbon isotopes.<ref name="BARC 5">{{cite web | url=https://worldwidescience.org/topicpages/b/barc.html|title= ISRAPS | publisher=ISRAPS |year=2007 | access-date=15 December 2007}}</ref>

His research spans from understanding quantum state-resolved study in molecular chemistry to the operation of optically pumped molecular lasers to its varied applications in [[photochemistry]] and also the isotope selective IR multiphoton dissociation in laser waveguide reactors. His work in radiochemistry addresses the radical chemistry of glucosamine naphthalene acetic acid and naphthalene acetic acids. His extensive work on [[Raman Spectroscopy]] addresses the process of how ions affect the structure of water.

In 2010, Sarkar was chosen as the [[Savitribai Phule Pune University]] Distinguished Lecturer in Photochemistry.<ref name="ISRAPS 5">{{cite web | url=http://www.israps.org.in/pdf/2009-Vol%2021-Issue%202-3.pdf| title= ISRAPS |publisher=ISRAPS |year=2009 | access-date=15 December 2009}}</ref>
